summary: Ran 31 backend integration tests (30 passed, 1 failed) covering auth, multi-tenant isolation, transactions with pending→approved flow, admin review, edit/audit, filters, receipts, reports math, insights, CSV+PDF exports for 5 kinds, admin-creates-UMKM, categories, forgot/reset/change password. Ran Playwright UI smoke: login (both roles), MSME dashboard metrics + charts, transaction dialog (IDR thousand separator working '150.000'), transaction created (pending), transactions list page with all data-testids present and 114 rows, filters panel, reports page presets/tabs/exports, admin dashboard (7 businesses inc. test data), admin review page with approve/reject buttons, audit log page rendering entries. Role-based routing enforced (MSME visiting /admin -> /dashboard; admin visiting /dashboard -> /admin). One CRITICAL multi-tenant isolation gap found in GET /api/transactions.

critical.issue: For non-admin users, the query-param business_id is silently ignored and the endpoint returns the caller's own transactions with HTTP 200 instead of 403. All other endpoints (/reports, /insights, /dashboard/business, /businesses/{id}, /categories) correctly return 403 via assert_business_access. This violates the strict multi-tenant contract stated in the spec ('...must all return 403').

action_items: In backend/server.py list_transactions(): when a non-admin passes ?business_id, call assert_business_access(user, business_id) instead of silently overwriting with user.business_id. Suggested fix: replace the else branch with `bid = business_id or user.get('business_id'); assert_business_access(user, bid); q['business_id'] = bid`.
Consider applying the same pattern to /api/audit-logs for consistency (currently also silently scopes to own business for non-admin).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py list_transactions leaks-no-data but silently masks cross-tenant probe attempts; should 403 explicitly to meet spec.
storage.py + receipts: signed-URL alternative pattern via ?auth_token= works but query-string tokens can leak via logs/referrer — acceptable for MVP.
CORS_ORIGINS='*' with allow_credentials=True is combined — Starlette will effectively drop credentials for wildcard origin; not blocking now but tighten before production.
seed_admin correctly updates existing admin password when env changes — good; no bcrypt.$ escape issues in .env.
Login endpoint uses per-IP+email brute-force lockout after 5 fails for 15 min (good). Note this can create false lockouts for tests running in parallel from same IP.
server.py is 768 lines — approaching the 700-line guideline; consider splitting transactions/reports/exports routers.
reports/insights correctly exclude pending & needs_correction (verified end-to-end).

success_rate.frontend: 100% smoke (all critical data-testids resolved on correct routes /transaksi /laporan /insight /pengaturan)

rca of the issue: TestIsolation.test_msme_cannot_read_other_business fails on /api/transactions only. In server.py list_transactions(), the code path is: `if user.role==admin: apply business_id filter if provided else no filter; else: q['business_id']=user.business_id` — meaning the incoming ?business_id query parameter is silently discarded for non-admin users. The MSME therefore gets HTTP 200 with their OWN data. No actual cross-tenant data leak occurs, BUT the spec explicitly requires 403 for this probe. Fix: `bid = body_business_id or user.business_id; assert_business_access(user, bid); q['business_id']=bid`. Reproduction: login as toko.maju@demo.id, GET /api/transactions?business_id=<kedai.nusantara business id> => expect 403, actual 200.
